trust.summaryTitle: About this assessment: method, score bands & FAQ

guide.methodologyDesc: This self-assessment explores perceived subjective tension across 5 core life dimensions: Work & Study, Health & Sleep, Personal Relationships, Financial Strain, and Daily Routine. Question weighting is structured around perceived situational burden (informed by Cohen's Perceived Stress Scale framework) to help users identify their single highest-friction domain rather than assign a diagnostic label.
guide.bandLowDesc: Manageable background tension. Focus on maintaining current recovery routines and healthy cognitive boundaries.
guide.bandModerateDesc: Accumulating strain in one or two domains. Prioritize targeted micro-breaks, daily task triage, and emotional offloading.
guide.bandHighDesc: Significant friction affecting focus or physical energy. We suggest taking our structured 7-day reset plan and adjusting daily workload demands.
guide.bandSevereDesc: Acute chronic fatigue or emotional exhaustion. We strongly recommend speaking with a licensed healthcare provider, counselor, or trusted medical support.
guide.faq1Q: Q: Is this test a formal medical diagnosis?
guide.faq1A: A: No. It is an educational self-reflection tool designed for personal awareness and lifestyle planning. Only licensed clinical professionals can evaluate or diagnose medical disorders.
guide.faq2Q: Q: Are my answers stored or shared?
guide.faq2A: A: Never. All calculations are executed 100% locally in your browser. No answers, scores, or categories are ever collected, logged, or sent to external servers.
guide.faq3Q: Q: How often should I take this assessment?
guide.faq3A: A: Once every 2 to 4 weeks, or whenever you experience significant life transitions, shifts in workload, or changes in personal routine.
guide.faq4Q: Q: How can I immediately reduce acute stress?
guide.faq4A: A: Physiological interventions such as cyclic physiological sighing (two quick inhales, slow extended exhale for 2 minutes) or brief 5-minute outdoor walking have been shown to rapidly downregulate autonomic arousal.
guide.faq5Q: Q: What should I do if my stress score is high?
guide.faq5A: A: Review your category breakdown to locate your primary friction source, use our private 7-day action plan to reduce cognitive overload, and consult healthcare professionals if distress interferes with basic daily tasks.
